scene: Day 150, gray winter morning: the river is frozen white from bank to bank around a tall stone water mill on its island, its big wooden wheel locked in ice and hung with icicles. A ring of pale light lies on the ice all around the island, with one narrow gap and a single glowing circle beside it. Outside the gap, on the ice, stands the Surveyor (mint-green head, blue shoulder stripe, scanner lowered) with the Worker's flat silver case at its feet. In the mill doorway, Reed (blue-gray scarf) and Mara (purple forearm band) stand in front; just behind them the Worker (plain alien, no case) is wrapped in a brown wool blanket, looking past them at the gap. What makes it scary: the safe water is gone, and the one-person gap is pointed at the alien hiding with them.

Day 130, ground floor of the stone mill, beside two huge round millstones and tall wooden gears, in pale snowy daylight from a small window: the Worker (plain mint-headed alien, no case) kneels on an empty flour sack, holding a pencil awkwardly in its glove over a long receipt roll covered in rows and rows of tiny joined circles drawn inside a long flat ship shape, with a curved arrow running up and off the paper. Reed (blue-gray scarf) and Mara (purple forearm band) crouch on either side, eyes wide, leaning in. Through the window, snow falls on the dark river. What makes it scary: the alien is finally answering where the pairs go, and the answer is a full ship.
